title: Apple launches research study to explore the use of AI for health

quotes.text: The Apple Health AI Usage Study is open to up to 200,000 eligible participants age 21 and older across the United States.
quotes.for: Participant cap, age requirement, and U.S. availability.

quotes.text: The study is designed from the ground up with privacy protections, transparency, and clinical guardrails, and study data will not be used to train AI models.
quotes.for: Privacy protections, guardrails, and no-training pledge.

quotes.text: The study app is not meant to diagnose or treat any condition, or replace the advice of medical professionals.
quotes.for: Non-diagnostic disclaimer for the study app.

quotes.text: At Apple, we believe responsible innovation starts with scientific rigor and clinical grounding.
quotes.for: Statement from Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple's vice president of Health and Fitness.

quotes.text: Patients and clinicians are both turning to AI, but the tools they use are being built and tested in separate worlds
quotes.for: Statement from Robert M. Wachter, M.D., chair of UCSF's Department of Medicine.

quotes.text: Consumer health technologies powered by LLMs may at times offer responses that are incomplete or unclear
quotes.for: Apple's stated rationale for the study.

quotes.text: To join, participants must have an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone (iPhone 15 Pro or later) running iOS 26 or later.
Apple has implemented security measures to protect the study data it maintains
quotes.for: Apple's only description of its security measures.

title: Apple launches new app to study how people use AI for health

quotes.text: The company is aiming to run this study with up to 200,000 participants for more than 12 months.
quotes.for: Planned study duration of more than 12 months.

quotes.text: The company said that OpenEvidence deletes the query and response data after 24 hours.
quotes.for: OpenEvidence's 24-hour deletion window for query and response data.

title: Apple Opens U.S. Study of Trust in Conversational Health AI

quotes.text: The App Store listing says the app can be used to understand symptoms or conditions, put personal health data in context, prepare for a medical visit, and build a personalized exercise or meal plan.
quotes.for: Use cases described in the App Store listing.

quotes.text: The App Store privacy label says user identifiers may be collected and linked to identity for analytics and app functionality, while diagnostics and performance data may be collected without being linked to identity.
quotes.for: App Store privacy label disclosures on linked identifiers.
